Let sN(x)=∑n=1N(1−x)xns_N(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{N}(1-x)x^nsN​(x)=∑n=1N​(1−x)xn for N≥1N \ge 1N≥1.

sN(x)=x(1−xN)↑x(0≤x<1),sN(1)=0s_N(x) = x(1-x^N) \uparrow x \quad (0 \le x < 1), \qquad s_N(1) = 0sN​(x)=x(1−xN)↑x(0≤x<1),sN​(1)=0
  • Dini's Theorem
Show solution

For x≠1x \ne 1x=1, ∑n=1Nxn=x(1−xN)1−x\sum_{n=1}^{N}x^n = \frac{x(1-x^N)}{1-x}∑n=1N​xn=1−xx(1−xN)​, so sN(x)=x(1−xN)s_N(x) = x(1-x^N)sN​(x)=x(1−xN) (the same formula holds at x=1x = 1x=1, where every term is 000). Each sNs_NsN​ is a polynomial, hence continuous, and sN+1(x)−sN(x)=(1−x)xN+1≥0s_{N+1}(x)-s_N(x) = (1-x)x^{N+1} \ge 0sN+1​(x)−sN​(x)=(1−x)xN+1≥0 (0≤x≤10 \le x \le 10≤x≤1), so sNs_NsN​ is monotone increasing.

  2. (a) For 0≤x≤a<10 \le x \le a < 10≤x≤a<1, xN→0x^N \to 0xN→0, so sN(x)→xs_N(x) \to xsN​(x)→x. The limit s(x)=xs(x) = xs(x)=x is continuous on [0,a][0,a][0,a]; a monotone increasing sequence of continuous functions converging pointwise to a continuous limit converges uniformly by Dini's theorem.

  3. (b) The pointwise limit on [0,1][0,1][0,1] is s(x)=xs(x) = xs(x)=x (x<1x < 1x<1), s(1)=0s(1) = 0s(1)=0, which is discontinuous at x=1x = 1x=1 (lim⁡x→1−s(x)=1≠0=s(1)\lim_{x\to 1^{-}}s(x) = 1 \ne 0 = s(1)limx→1−​s(x)=1=0=s(1)). A uniform limit of continuous functions must be continuous, so convergence on [0,1][0,1][0,1] cannot be uniform.
